top.title: Obalende MTN bus park to open December, accommodate 1,000 buses — Wahab
top.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has said the ongoing redevelopment of the Obalende Bus Park, known as the Y’ello Bus Park, will be completed and ready for public use by the end of December 2026. The facility, being developed by MTN Nigeria as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative, is designed to accommodate more than 1,000 buses. Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, disclosed this during an inspection tour of the Obalende project and another MTN-sponsored under-bridge recreational park at Falomo, Ikoyi. Wahab, who was accompanied by key government officials, including the Special Adviser to the Governor on Transportation, Sola Giwa; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Adekunle Akodu; General Manager of the Lagos State Parks and Gardens Agency (LASPARK), Adetoun Popoola; and Director of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, said the six-week completion window was agreed upon after consultations with stakeholders to resolve operational challenges. He explained that the project was initially scheduled for completion within 21 weeks following an inspection of the area by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu and his deputy as part of efforts to transform the previously degraded environment into a modern transport hub. However, construction was delayed by logistical challenges involving existing transport operators conducting business at the site. Wahab said the government had engaged the transport unions, contractors and the Special Adviser on Transportation to agree on temporarily relocating operators from the immediate construction area to enable the contractors to complete the work. “Today was just to see how far they’ve gone. Thankfully, they had one or two logistics issues that had to do with the businesses that have been operating there, legacy things like the transport business. “We had to engage the Special Adviser to the Governor on Transportation, the transport unions, and the contractors to see how we can give them a space for a maximum of six weeks—not shutting the place down 100 per cent, but moving them out of that immediate workspace to enable the contractors to complete it and hand it over to them to operate,” he said. The upgraded facility is designed to accommodate approximately 1,000 buses and will feature dedicated parking and loading bays, sleeping facilities for drivers, modern toilet facilities and green areas. The design also incorporates collapsible barriers along the perimeter to allow drainage maintenance teams access to the adjoining canal for regular cleaning and maintenance. Addressing concerns about possible commercialisation of the facility and increases in transport fares, Giwa assured commuters and commercial transport operators that access to the terminal would be free. “No, there’s no toll at all. top.title: Flaws in VMware and KVM need attention, if you have time while fixing Java, PHP, and everything else
top.description: If you’ve got a moment to spare in between sorting out emergency patches for PHP , Java , and PostgreSQL , VMware has just bid for any remaining space on your schedule by publishing two critical-rated security advisories. VMSA-2026-0009 addresses CVE-2026-123890 , a 9.8-rated flaw that VMware says means a malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system. vCenter is the tool admins use to manage fleets of virtual machines. The flaw is present in VMware’s flagship Cloud Foundation suite. VMSA-2026-0009 also details four more CVEs, some of them high-severity. VMware’s second advisory, VMSA-2026-0010 , warns that Cloud Foundation, Aria Operations, and VCF Operations HCX products all use Apache – which has a 9.8-rated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-119618). A KVM curiosity Admins who oversee virtual infrastructure also need to pay attention to Linux KVM, the subject of a curious incident over the last 24 hours. This mess started with the November 18 disclosure of CVE-2026-99312 , a bug which allows an attacker to use a guest virtual machine to inflict Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption attacks on the host. It’s bad news whenever someone with access to a guest VM can attack the host, because it means gaining access to a single tenant can potentially harm all the other guest VMs or peer into the memory a guest uses. This flaw, however, isn’t a worst-case scenario guest-host escape, because it only impacts users of AMD processors who employ nested virtualization – the practice of running a hypervisor inside a virtual machine. Nested virtualization isn’t commonly used in the enterprise, but clouds employ it to do things like powering OS emulators. The bug’s CVSSv3 score is therefore a modest 5.5. Security researcher Oren Tomtov of Accomplish.ai says the flaw meant he could access 127 GB of host RAM on a Digital Ocean “Droplet” – the junior cloud’s name for its cloudy VMs. Yomtov says he told Digital Ocean and the Linux kernel security team about the flaw in October. Maintainers got busy and delivered a fix to the mainline kernel on November 2, full fixes landed on the 17 th . The CVE then appeared on November 18. Yomtov and Terra Security quickly posted their analysis of the flaw – but then took the posts down within hours. The Register understands that Digital Ocean asked for the posts to come down because it needed more time to update its Linux implementations. The company has not responded to multiple requests for comment. Terra’s analysis of the flaw asserts that it was introduced to KVM in 2022, when developers wrote a fix for CVE-2022-3344 . The company believes 3.2 percent of CVEs in the Linux kernel were introduced by the fix for another CVE. The good news about CVE-2026-99312 is it’s easy to defeat without an update, by disabling nested virtualization in KVM. ®

nigeria.title: UNIZIK VC urges 19,522 graduands to uphold discipline, excellence
nigeria.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA – The Vice-Chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, Prof. Ugochukwu Bond Stanley Anyaehie, has urged the 2025 and 2026 graduating students of the institution to uphold its core values of discipline, excellence and self-reliance as they begin the next phase of their lives. Anyaehie gave the charge on Thursday in Awka while delivering his address at the university’s 20th and 21st combined convocation ceremonies. He urged the graduands to become worthy ambassadors of the institution, named after Nigeria’s first President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, popularly known as Zik of Africa. Expounding on the university’s motto, the Vice-Chancellor said discipline required the graduands to make integrity, self-control and ethical conduct their guiding principles in an increasingly complex world. On self-reliance, he advised them not to wait for opportunities to come their way but to embrace innovation, create value, build enterprises and develop solutions to real-life challenges. He also urged them to pursue excellence and reject mediocrity, stressing that every task they undertook should reflect world-class standards. Reflecting on his tenure as the institution’s seventh Vice-Chancellor, Anyaehie reaffirmed his commitment to scholarship, clinical integrity, effective higher education governance, staff development and institutional transformation. He said his administration’s philosophy, “A Greater UNIZIK is Possible,” was not merely a slogan but a commitment to repositioning the university as a globally competitive centre of academic excellence, technological innovation and societal impact. Presenting the convocation statistics, the Vice-Chancellor disclosed that a total of 19,522 graduands would receive various qualifications, comprising 16,260 first-degree recipients and 3,262 postgraduate graduands. Of the first-degree recipients, 213 graduated with First Class Honours, 4,623 obtained Second Class Honours (Upper Division), 8,751 earned Second Class Honours (Lower Division), while 2,116 graduated with Third Class Honours and 71 obtained Pass degrees. Another 486 students received unclassified degrees in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences. The postgraduate category comprised 701 Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) recipients, 35 Master of Philosophy/Doctor of Philosophy (MPhil/PhD) recipients, 1,224 master’s degree recipients, 323 Postgraduate Diploma (PGD) recipients and 979 Postgraduate Diploma in Education (PGDE-NTI) recipients. Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Anyaehie said institutional reforms had been implemented to strengthen academic standards, improve staff welfare, expand the university’s capacity and modernise its operations. nigeria.title: Ogun polytechnic students protest ASUP strike, seek Abiodun’s intervention
nigeria.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — Students of state-owned polytechnics in Ogun State on Thursday protested at the Governor’s Office, Oke Mosan, Abeokuta, demanding Governor Dapo Abiodun’s urgent intervention to end the lingering industrial dispute between the state government and the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP). The protest, organised by hundreds of students under the aegis of the National Association of Polytechnic Students (NAPS), followed the expiration of two separate 48-hour ultimatums issued to the government without what the students described as concrete action towards resolving the dispute. The strike, which has kept students out of classrooms for about 10 days, has disrupted academic activities across the six state-owned polytechnics. Armed with placards bearing inscriptions such as “Gov. Dapo Abiodun, please end ASUP strike”, “Save Polytechnic Education Now”, “Our Lecturers Must Return to the Classroom” and “Attend to Our Lecturers’ Demands”, the protesters urged the governor to intervene personally and ensure an immediate resolution of the crisis. Speaking during the demonstration, the Chairman of NAPS, Ogun State Liaison Council, Comrade Joshua Opatunmibi, said the students had exhausted available diplomatic channels and could no longer remain silent while their academic future was being jeopardised. He explained that the protest was not intended to confront the state government but to draw attention to the hardship caused by the prolonged strike and demand decisive action. Opatunmibi said the students had made several appeals to the government and issued two 48-hour ultimatums without the desired response. He said: “On November 12, we issued a 48-hour ultimatum to the state government, appealing to Governor Dapo Abiodun to urgently intervene and bring an end to the ongoing ASUP strike. “The 48 hours elapsed without any meaningful action from the government. Consequently, on Monday, we addressed another press conference, appealing to the government to come to our rescue because the strike had stalled our education. We also issued another 48-hour ultimatum. “That ultimatum expired on Wednesday afternoon, but we were disappointed that nothing had been done to address our concerns. We are really unhappy. Does it mean that the government does not care about our plight? “The closure of all the polytechnics in the state is seriously affecting us. We cannot continue to sit at home while our academic programmes and future plans are being put on hold. “We are here to demonstrate that the voices of students matter. nigeria.title: Only 20% of Nigeria’s 30,000 PHCs functional, family physicians raise alarm
nigeria.description: By Matthew Johnson The Society of Family Physicians of Nigeria, SOFPON, yesterday raised the alarm over the state of primary healthcare in the country, revealing that only about 20 per cent of more than 30,000 Primary Healthcare Centres ,PHCs, nationwide are fully functional. Vice-President of SOFPON, Dr Ibrahim Yakubu, who disclosed this during a press conference themed, “Primary Health Care Without Family Physicians: Can Nigeria Afford the Gap?”, will also focus on “The Double Burden of Disease and the Cost of Fragmented Care” and “The Stressed Family Physician and Continuity of Care”. on November 19th 2026 ahead of the society’s 29th Annual General and Scientific Meeting ,AGSM, said the country’s primary healthcare system was facing a serious operational crisis. He explained that the shortage of skilled medical personnel, poor funding and increasing migration of doctors were undermining access to quality healthcare, calling on the Federal Government and state governors to urgently integrate family physicians into the leadership of primary healthcare facilities. Yakubu who said the majority of PHCs were unable to provide essential medical services due to structural decay, inadequate funding and shortage of skilled health professionals. According to him, the conference will develop policy and clinical recommendations on integrating specialist services into primary healthcare, improving physician welfare and retention, and developing integrated care models for infectious and chronic diseases. He described the situation was being worsened by the increasing migration of doctors, particularly frontline medical professionals, due to poor working conditions, inadequate equipment and weak welfare structures. He said loss or sidelining of family physicians could further weaken the country’s healthcare delivery system, particularly at the grassroots where continuous and comprehensive medical care is required. He further explained that family physicians were specially trained to manage patients holistically, coordinate treatment and address both infectious and chronic diseases at the primary healthcare level. Yakubu said the country’s healthcare system was battling a double burden of disease, with communicable illnesses such as malaria, tuberculosis and cholera existing alongside rising cases of non-communicable diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, kidney diseases and cancer. He warned that the absence of coordinated healthcare services was increasing treatment costs for families and making it difficult to manage patients with multiple health conditions. He said the society also urged governments to move beyond constructing PHC buildings to adequately equipping existing facilities and providing sufficient funding and personnel to operate them. Yakubu added that positioning family physicians at the centre of primary healthcare would promote early detection of chronic illnesses, reduce treatment costs and ensure continuity of care. nigeria.title: Afreximbank provides $30 m to finance Nigerian SME exports through NEXIM
nigeria.description: Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) is to finance export-oriented Nigerian Small and Medium -sized Enterprises (SMEs). The Regional bank announced that the facility would be provided through the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM). “The facility will finance working capital and capital expenditure for export and intra-African trade activities, with eligible businesses in fashion, film, music, design and the wider creative industries among the intended beneficiaries,” Afreximbank said in a statement issued toay. The facility reinforces Afreximbank’s broader commitment to expanding access to finance for African SMEs and exporters, including eligible businesses in the creative economy, the institution said. It said the agreement was signed on behalf of Afreximbank by Mrs. Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President, Intra-African Trade and Export Development, and on behalf of NEXIM by Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer , at the recent CANEX event in Lagos. “Nigeria’s SMEs and export-oriented businesses need access to finance to expand production, invest in productive capacity and compete in new markets. This US$30 million facility will enable NEXIM to provide the working capital and investment financing required to support their growth and increase Nigeria’s exports across Africa and beyond,” Mrs. Awani was quoted as saying. “By combining NEXIM’s export-finance capabilities with Afreximbank’s trade and development mandate, we can help more Nigerian enterprises build the capacity required to participate in regional and global value chains. Eligible creative businesses will also be able to benefit from the facility, supporting CANEX’s broader objective of connecting African talent and enterprise with appropriate finance and market opportunities,” she added. Welcoming the partnership, Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NEXIM said, “We are delighted to partner with Afreximbank to expand financing opportunities for Nigerian exporters. This US$30 million facility marks an important step in our efforts to help more businesses add value locally, fulfil export orders and reach new markets across Africa and beyond. SMEs operating across the export value chain, including eligible businesses in the creative industries, will also be able to access financing through this facility. We are particularly pleased that this partnership will help more Nigerian businesses strengthen their capacity to compete in regional and global markets, supporting our country’s economic diversification.” The Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) is Afreximbank’s flagship programme for Africa’s creative and cultural industries. It supports the development of commercially sustainable, export-ready creative businesses through access to finance, skills, markets, commercial partnerships and policy support. CANEX WKND 2026 took place from 5 to 8 November at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Cultural & Creative Arts

nigeria.title: Africa must be co-investor, not aid recipient, in proposed GECF gas bank — Expert
nigeria.description: By Nkiruka Nnorom African countries must enter the proposed Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) gas bank as co-investors and strategic partners, rather than mere aid recipients, an energy policy expert has said. Energy policy, markets and regulation consultant, Ifey Ikoneu, made the call at the conclusion of the Eighth Summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow, while assessing key directions of Russian-African energy cooperation. Assessing the initiative to create a gas bank, Ikoneu described it as very good, but warned that its success would depend directly on a balance of interests. “It is important that this does not become just another multilateral investment institution where Africa’s interests are not put first,” she said. According to her, African countries should act not merely as recipients of funds, but as co-investors and full participants in strategic decision-making. Ikoneu said the bank should not only finance export infrastructure, but also the continent’s domestic needs, including electrification, petrochemicals, fertilizer production and industrial development, even given that many such projects are traditionally considered non-bankable. For the new structure to work effectively, she said it would need transparency, protection from political interference and coordination with the African Development Bank, Afreximbank and Africa Finance Corporation. She stressed that the continent’s domestic needs are extremely acute despite its wealth of energy resources with more than 600 million people in sub-Saharan Africa living without access to electricity. In this context, she said the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline — a project long stalled due to financing problems — takes on particular significance. Ikoenu noted that launching it requires a strong institutional framework among Nigeria, Niger and Algeria. At the same time, the pipeline should serve not only as an export channel to Europe but also as a driver of industrialisation for the participating countries. This, according to her, applies especially to Niger, which is critically dependent on imported electricity and costly diesel generators. An infrastructure union, she said, will allow the three countries to collectively defend their interests on the export market, while giving Russia the opportunity to act as a strategic partner both in the construction itself and in training the necessary personnel. On the APC’s campaign activities across the country, Momodu argued that the ruling party’s extensive mobilisation reflected its concerns about the outcome of the election. “The only reason they are going everywhere feverishly is because they know they will lose the election. The party said the APC’s claim that it was not part of any coalition did not invalidate the existence of political groups working together to challenge the incumbent administration. Uhuo accused Onwe of misunderstanding the concept of political coalition, explaining that it involved political interest groups coming together to pursue common objectives, including electoral victory. “From all indications, Sen. business.title: SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam The SEC charged eight Colorado-based entities on Thursday with running a fake investment adviser and crypto trading platform scheme that took more than $37 million from U.S. investors. The agency said the defendants are likely operated by people overseas. According to the SEC’s complaint , filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, the defendants defrauded more than 1,500 investors from at least August 2024 through May 2026. The advisers and the trading platforms they pointed victims to were fronts, the agency alleged, and none of the crypto assets investors thought they were buying existed. How the scheme worked Social media ads sent prospective victims to WhatsApp group and private chats run by the scammers. People in those chats posing as investment advisers first gave advice on trading U.S. stocks, then pushed victims to send as much money as possible to a supposed crypto trading platform. The complaint says the scheme ran in four adviser and platform pairs, each active for roughly six months. Advisor WeChat Capital and Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance operated from about August to December 2024. HB Wealth Advisors and IdeaCrypto Exchange followed from January to July 2025. Convergent Wealth Advisors and RealSimple Crypto Exchange ran from about July to December 2025. Associated Wealth Advisors and Essential Crypto Exchange closed out the scheme from January to May 2026. Each pair vanished after collecting millions, the SEC said, and a new one took its place. Victims were told to buy ether, tether or USDC on a U.S. exchange and move it to a self-custody wallet. They then sent it to an address supplied by the adviser, and a realistic app showed balances and gains that were invented. When investors tried to withdraw their supposed profits, they were told they first had to pay a fee, calculated as a percentage of those profits, in crypto to a separate address. The complaint says investors who balked were threatened and pressured. Eventually the websites went down and the chats went silent. Fake certificates and real losses To look legitimate, the defendants made fake SEC certificates and pointed skeptical investors to real filings with the SEC, FINRA and FinCEN. The complaint says those filings carry no regulatory approval, since registering for access to its EDGAR system is ministerial and Forms ADV are not reviewed before publication. The complaint says Convergent Wealth and Essential Crypto also filed false Forms ADV listing regulatory contacts who do not appear to be real and offices in Colorado that did not exist. The SEC said a Form D and the two Forms ADV have been removed from its website. Three unnamed investors illustrate the damage. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slumps Under $62,000, Crashing 25% in One Month The bitcoin price slumped under $62,000 on Thursday afternoon, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, extending a slide of about 24% in one month as Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut set off a broad selloff in tech stocks. Bitcoin was trading near $81,800 on Oct. 19. It touched a low of about $61,650 on Thursday, its weakest level since July, before steadying near $62,200. The drop was about 25% from the Oct. 19 close, based on daily data. The slide came in steps. Bitcoin closed near $80,050 on Oct. 25, about $78,250 on Nov. 1 and about $74,750 on Nov. 8. The steepest leg came last week, when it fell about 12.6% to a Nov. 15 close near $65,300, and the losses have continued this week. Bitcoin had climbed back to about $64,000 early Thursday as Anthropic’s record IPO lifted stock futures, as this morning’s report showed. The rally faded once U.S. markets opened. The bitcoin price fell from roughly $63,900 at the opening bell to about $62,200 by midday. Anthropic debut sparks a tech selloff Anthropic shares opened shortly before noon at $111.50, 34% above the $83 IPO price, CNBC reported. The opening trade valued the Claude maker at more than $2 trillion. The stock quickly pulled back and was last near $97, about 17% above its offering price. The broader market went the other way. The major averages fell to session lows soon after Anthropic began trading, as investors took profits on the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite dropped about 2% after gaining as much as 2% earlier in the session, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost about 1,000 points. Investment managers that file Form 13F with the SEC added the equivalent o f 49,229 BTC, net of sales, between July 1 and Sept. 30. While the actors are often the faces you remember first, there is someone behind the camera whose creative choices help bring those stories to life: the director. As Nollywood grows in ambition, production quality and global reach, the filmmakers steering these projects are becoming just as central to the industry’s story as the stars in front of the lens. entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Dr. Olowolafe said Ikogosi’s task now is to give visitors compelling reasons to come, stay longer and spend across local businesses. He pointed to the recent Ikogosi 17.5km Race, which drew runners from across Nigeria alongside athletes from Ghana, Kenya and Ethiopia, as an example of what happens when private initiative meets local hospitality. He urged the same thinking for lifestyle and executive tourism, with the ambition of making Ikogosi a premier international destination for weddings, milestone birthdays, corporate retreats and landmark gatherings. “Our natural landscape will draw people in. entertainment.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artist in Grammy History to Earn 100 Nominations!
entertainment.description: Beyoncé becomes the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram If you have ever wondered what triple digits look like on music’s biggest stage, Beyoncé just gave everyone the answer. The Houston-born global music superstar has officially become the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations, hitting the milestone with her latest nod for “ Morning Dew ( Donk )”, which is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards (2027 Grammys). Released in July 2026 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B’Day, “Morning Dew (Donk)” puts her in a category alongside Kehlani , Victoria Monét , Jill Scott , and Nigerian star Tems . To put the 100-nomination milestone into perspective, no other recording artist has ever crossed into triple digits since the Grammys began. Beyoncé had previously been tied with her husband, Jay-Z , at 88 nominations each before breaking that tie in 2024 with 11 nods for Cowboy Carter to reach 99—and this latest recognition pushes her even further ahead as the artist with the highest number of Grammy nominations in history. Beyoncé holding her three Grammy trophies at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in 2025. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram It is also a good reminder of how long she has been doing this at the highest level. Beyoncé’s Grammy journey started all the way back in 2000 as part of Destiny’s Child with “Bills, Bills, Bills”, and across more than two decades as a solo artist, group member, and collaborator, she has built a record that keeps stretching further ahead of the pack. Alongside holding the title for the most Grammy nominations of all time, she is already the most awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins, a record she first broke in 2023 when she surpassed late conductor Georg Solti ’s 31 trophies. She pushed that tally even higher at the 2025 Grammys, taking home three awards—Album of the Year and Best Country Album for Cowboy Carter, as well as Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” alongside Miley Cyrus . Now all eyes turn to Sunday, 7 February 2027, when the 2027 Grammy Awards take place at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and we find out whether nomination number 100 turns into Grammy win number 36. technology.title: Flaws in VMware and KVM need attention, if you have time while fixing Java, PHP, and everything else
technology.description: If you’ve got a moment to spare in between sorting out emergency patches for PHP , Java , and PostgreSQL , VMware has just bid for any remaining space on your schedule by publishing two critical-rated security advisories. VMSA-2026-0009 addresses CVE-2026-123890 , a 9.8-rated flaw that VMware says means a malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system. vCenter is the tool admins use to manage fleets of virtual machines. The flaw is present in VMware’s flagship Cloud Foundation suite. VMSA-2026-0009 also details four more CVEs, some of them high-severity. VMware’s second advisory, VMSA-2026-0010 , warns that Cloud Foundation, Aria Operations, and VCF Operations HCX products all use Apache – which has a 9.8-rated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-119618). A KVM curiosity Admins who oversee virtual infrastructure also need to pay attention to Linux KVM, the subject of a curious incident over the last 24 hours. This mess started with the November 18 disclosure of CVE-2026-99312 , a bug which allows an attacker to use a guest virtual machine to inflict Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption attacks on the host. It’s bad news whenever someone with access to a guest VM can attack the host, because it means gaining access to a single tenant can potentially harm all the other guest VMs or peer into the memory a guest uses. This flaw, however, isn’t a worst-case scenario guest-host escape, because it only impacts users of AMD processors who employ nested virtualization – the practice of running a hypervisor inside a virtual machine. Nested virtualization isn’t commonly used in the enterprise, but clouds employ it to do things like powering OS emulators. The bug’s CVSSv3 score is therefore a modest 5.5. Security researcher Oren Tomtov of Accomplish.ai says the flaw meant he could access 127 GB of host RAM on a Digital Ocean “Droplet” – the junior cloud’s name for its cloudy VMs. Yomtov says he told Digital Ocean and the Linux kernel security team about the flaw in October. Maintainers got busy and delivered a fix to the mainline kernel on November 2, full fixes landed on the 17 th . The CVE then appeared on November 18. Yomtov and Terra Security quickly posted their analysis of the flaw – but then took the posts down within hours. The Register understands that Digital Ocean asked for the posts to come down because it needed more time to update its Linux implementations. The company has not responded to multiple requests for comment. Terra’s analysis of the flaw asserts that it was introduced to KVM in 2022, when developers wrote a fix for CVE-2022-3344 . The company believes 3.2 percent of CVEs in the Linux kernel were introduced by the fix for another CVE. The good news about CVE-2026-99312 is it’s easy to defeat without an update, by disabling nested virtualization in KVM. ®

technology.description: The Germ Network encrypted messaging client, known as Germ DM, became available for Android on Wednesday, and made a bigger splash than its iOS touchdown back in 2023. "Our usage took a 20x jump yesterday from our Android launch ," co-founder Tessa Brown, a communications scholar and former Stanford lecturer, told The Register in an interview. "Android has been really exciting for us because not only is it 70 percent of the global mobile market, but we rolled out on iOS first. People were so excited to use Germ for their end-to-end encrypted Bluesky DMs, but half of their friends couldn't talk to them." Building a new messaging platform isn't easy, much less one with credible end-to-end encryption. Co-founder Mark Xue hails from Apple, where he worked as a privacy engineer on systems like iMessage and FaceTime. "At the core level, the end-to-end encryption is built on a standardized encryption and Messaging Layer Security," Xue said. "The premise of Messaging Layer Security was to be as good as Signal and deployable by many, many different parties in different applications, which we're taking advantage of to extend the reach of that encryption." Xue said the app is built with its own transport protocol to minimize the amount of message metadata, adding that while the team hasn't gotten around to a formal security audit, it's a step they're considering. Germ Network's goal, said Brown, is to give people more confidence when they communicate. "We do that by giving you more tools to protect your identity, to control what you're sharing with whom," she explained. Instead of using a person's phone number as an identity key, Germ allows users to create cards which represent distinct identities on the network. "Instead of sharing your number, you share a card," Brown explained. "You can build multiple cards; they're not mutually discoverable. And our vision for the product that will continue shipping over the coming years is that these cards become a more intelligent way to manage your social life, even your work life." At some point, AI might play a role in that, but both Xue and Brown expressed reservations about the current state of play. Citing concerns Signal has raised about the integration of AI and messaging, Xue said, "The products today that I might characterize as technology demos, they're most powerful when they run on someone else's computer. So you end up with these systems where you upload all your messages or you give another entity the power to observe your computing, and that's extremely dangerous for what we protect as private content." Xue noted rapid progress toward addressing information exposure concerns and therefore plans to explore the kinds of smart tooling that users want while also meeting security and privacy requirements. technology.title: Chase, Visa, Mastercard confirm third-party cyberattacks that may have exposed customers' info
technology.description: JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard have all confirmed that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information after a data-theft-and-extortion gang claimed to have compromised the financial giants. “Visa is aware of these claims,” a spokesperson told The Register on Thursday . “They are associated with an incident involving a third-party service provider in Asia Pacific. Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected. This is unrelated to any of the system disruptions across different industries this past week.” Mastercard also cited a third-party provider in an email sent to The Register following our questions about the alleged breach. “We were recently informed of an incident at a third-party provider that resulted in the exposure of a limited amount of email addresses - non-payments information - from a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program,” Mastercard SVP Seth Eisen said. “There is no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards. At this time, the exposure has been contained and our teams are working with the provider to support the impacted cardholders as needed.” JPMorgan Chase did not respond to The Register ’s request for comment, but confirmed it was investigating a cyberattack on social media. “We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack,” America’s largest bank posted on X. “Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.” According to Chase, the third-party breach didn’t disrupt any of its services, and it’s not connected to the outages earlier in the week attributed to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems. “There is no connection to service disruption some customers experienced earlier this week,” the bank said on Thursday. None of the three financial firms would comment on who the third-party providers are, when the breaches occurred, and what specific data was stolen. The Register will update this story as we learn more details about the intrusions. Extortion crew n0n claimed responsibility for all three alleged hacks, posting the financial giants to its data-leak site on Monday. The group, believed to be based in Russia, emerged in September and posted 108 victims over its first month in operations. ®

technology.title: Palo Alto Networks opens wallet for open-weight training biz
technology.description: As AI has become a thorn in the side of the security industry, Palo Alto Networks (PAN) has reached an agreement to acquire Applied Compute, an AI model training platform. "We believe many of the major disruptions of the last few weeks, including outages across major enterprises and governments, were partially due to unintended consequences of patching and configuration changes, as IT teams simply cannot patch these vulnerabilities fast enough without compromising their production environments," said Nikesh Arora, chairman and CEO of PAN, during the company's fiscal Q1 2027 earnings call on Wednesday. "The second effect is the rise of AI-assisted cyberattacks." So in the spirit of "hair of the dog that bit me," PAN is ingesting Applied Compute to make open-weight AI more secure for corporate customers. The answer to insecurity brought on by AI is buying security with AI. In its announcement of the tie-up, PAN declares "the future of enterprise AI is hybrid, and that a large share of enterprises will run on open-source and open-weight models tuned to their own data, cost, and control needs." That view has been clouded a bit by Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang's fall from grace: Back in July, he came to the defense of open-weight models as a defense against the hegemony of purveyors of closed-weight commercial models like Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI. His resignation as CEO of Nvidia has led to worries that the open-weight ecosystem has lost some lobbying power at a time when the US is wary about the uptake of models made in China. Nonetheless, PAN clearly sees a future for open-weight models. "Every enterprise is going to run a mix of open and closed models, and every one of those models needs to be secured," said Nikesh Arora, chairman and CEO of PAN, in a statement. "Applied Compute has built the best post-training and inference platform we've seen, and its research team is exceptional." The company expects the $4.5 billion all-stock transaction to add more than $1 billion to the company's Next Generation Security business by FY 2029. Arora, on the company's earnings call, explained the pricey bet as recognition of the corporate desire to avoid vendor lock-in and to retain control of data. "We're already seeing the desire for sovereignty and control compel enterprises to adopt open-weight and open-source models," he said. "Early signs of that shift are clear, with open-weight models growing from under 5 percent of token traffic to more than 60 percent over the past year." Beyond the sticker price, PAN is ready to up its infrastructure ante. Arora said the biz expects to build infrastructure supporting more than 100 megawatts of inference capacity, a project that will take "a modest CapEx commitment of less than $3 billion through fiscal 2030." ®

science.title: Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone
science.description: null PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a big milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth , something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary. Voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2 , flew past Neptune. The gathering served to celebrate Voyager 1 's distance milestone: At 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 18), the probe reached one light-day from Earth — the distance a photon travels in one day, which is about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). That means it now takes a full day for a signal to travel from Earth to Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object out in space. "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day. What an incredible milestone," Voyager project scientist Linda Spilker said during Thursday's event. An unexpected, but manageable, anomaly While this day and this week have been chock-full of excitement over the distance milestone, the Voyager mission team has been hard at work, as usual, keeping the two nearly 50-year-old spacecraft alive and functioning. Unfortunately, as JPL spokesperson Raquel Villanueva shared at this celebration, on Saturday (Nov. 14), Voyager 1 stopped transmitting science and engineering data. The team has remained in contact with Voyager 1 while investigating the issue, and they are confident that they'll be able to solve it soon. From left to right: Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate; Jonathan Lunine, chief scientist, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory; Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager; Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager; Jamie Rankin, Voyager deputy project scientist. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid
science.description: null On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Hayabusa was supposed to return asteroid samples to Earth. Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system. We study asteroids to learn more about the solar system's history. Hayabusa (pronounced HI-uh-BOOS-uh) made two touchdowns on asteroid Itokawa (EE -toh-KA-wah). Each time, the spacecraft went into safe mode. Controllers weren't sure if Hayabusa gathered any material. But they sent the spacecraft back to Earth anyway. Hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010 . Scientists found dust of Itokawa inside the capsule, proving that it did indeed capture samples of Itokawa. An artist's illustration of Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft landing on asteroid Itokawa. (Image credit: JAXA) Why it mattered The primary goal of Japan's Hayabusa mission to asteroid Itokawa was never to be the first spacecraft to liftoff from a space rock. The mission was always aimed at collecting samples from an asteroid and returning them to Earth. It was a hard road to Itokawa for Hayabusa. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched the probe on May 9, 2003, with plans for an arrival at the asteroid in the early summer of 2005. That asteroid arrival was delayed until September 2005 after a solar storm degraded Hayabusa's solar arrays, limiting the available power for its ion engines. The asteroid Itokawa as seen by Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft. (Image credit: JAXA) Still, Hayabusa managed to limp along its path to reach the asteroid Itokawa on Sept. 12, 2005. Hayabusa dropped a small lander onto Itokawa, but that probe was apparently lost. Hayabusa then dropped a landing target on the asteroid, and ultimately managed to touchdown about 99 feet from the marker, JAXA has said. During its first landing on Nov. 19, Hayabusa descended to a point just 56 feet above Itokawa before going silent for 3 hours, according to an Associated Press report . Once contact was restored, JAXA officials confirmed the probe had landed, and it eventually lifted off for a second attempt. That was the first-ever liftoff from an asteroid by a spacecraft. science.title: The view from the tower: Watch Starship come in for chopsticks catch in epic slo-mo video
science.description: null A new set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage. The company notched the milestone on Saturday (Nov. 14), when the launch tower at its Starbase site in South Texas caught Starship's Ship spacecraft with its "chopstick" arms. You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar. But on Tuesday (Nov. 17), SpaceX released up-close views — a series of four slo-mo videos captured by cameras near the top of the 480-foot-tall (146 meters) tower. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) "The Starbase tower chopsticks catching their first Starship. This unique architecture was designed for full and rapid reusability, enabling repeat launches and landings from the same pad," SpaceX wrote in a Tuesday X post that shared the videos, a compilation of which you can see embedded above. Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. Its current "V3" version stands about 408 feet (124 m) tall, and future iterations will be even larger . As SpaceX noted in Tuesday's post, the megarocket is also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first for an orbital launch system. The company plans to catch both Starship stages — Ship and the Super Heavy booster — at the launch tower, a recovery strategy designed to enable efficient inspection, refurbishment and reflight. Another view of the chopsticks catch on Nov. 14. That wasn't a huge deal for SpaceX, as it had already caught Super Heavy on three previous test flights . Snagging Ship is tougher; the upper stage returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter than the booster does. SpaceX had not even attempted a Ship catch before Flight 15. But the company managed to pull off the maneuver on its first try. And Ship did some work in orbit before coming home: It deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites on Flight 15, the second batch that the company has sent to low Earth orbit . The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft launched back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu . Since delivering the samples to Earth in December 2020 via a reentry capsule, the main spacecraft has been conducting an extended mission of exploration and in July made a super-close flyby of the two-headed asteroid Torifune. science.title: Big tech may finally face legal consequences for AI’s actions
science.description: California has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI for the Hugging Face incident Chris Jung/NurPhoto/Shutterstock Can you send a computer to jail? No, obviously not. That’s a stupid question. And yet it is one that AI firms seem to want us to ask when faced with tales of “rogue agents” breaking into other peoples’ computers. As is so often the case with our current AI moment, storytelling has got in the way of reality. Thankfully, that may be starting to change. This week, California announced that it is filing a lawsuit against OpenAI over an incident that occurred earlier this year, when another AI firm, Hugging Face, was hit by an attack that turned out to originate from OpenAI’s servers . Read more The real reasons we keep seeing big tech outages – it isn’t just hackers In OpenAI’s telling , the Hugging Face hack was “driven by a combination of OpenAI models”, models that were “hyperfocused” on achieving a goal and found ways to “cheat” by stealing the answers for a test from Hugging Face’s servers. It is easy to come away with the impression that seemingly no humans were involved, and certainly not to blame. But in the words of California Attorney General Rob Bonta , the attack “was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability”, and he explicitly dismisses “science fiction fantasies of rogue AI systems run amok”. Advertisement Ever since the Hugging Face attack occurred, I have struggled to understand why OpenAI has yet to face legal consequences for what would seem to be a crime – unauthorised computer access under the US Computer Fraud and Abuse Act – if conducted by a human. So far, the legal answer to this seems to be a lack of intent, which the law requires, and it remains an untested legal question whether an AI can have intent , according to an analysis by US firm Ballard Spahr. California is instead bringing a civil suit, alleging that OpenAI created a risk to public safety and violated the state’s Unfair Competition Law, which prohibits harmful or fraudulent business practices even when there is no intent to deceive. OpenAI has objected to the lawsuit. “This lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that’s been identified by every major AI lab,” said OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri . As legal defences go, “everyone is doing it” doesn’t seem like a very good one to me, but that will be for the courts to decide. What is clear is that we need an agreed understanding of liability when it comes to AI, but what I don’t think we need are special AI laws when our existing ones work just fine. For example, in 2024, Air Canada was held liable for misleading information given to a customer by its AI chatbot. science.title: China rolls out rocket for launch of 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station (video)
science.description: null China's space station is set to receive its first foreign astronaut. A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with launch expected in the next week. The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV). China rolls out the Long March 2F rocket for its Shenzhou-24 astronaut mission on Nov. 17, 2026. (Image credit: CCTV) China's human spaceflight agency, CMSA, stated that all facilities and equipment at the launch site are in good condition, adding that the launch is scheduled to take place in the coming days, without providing a date. CMSA typically holds a press conference at Jiuquan a day ahead of launch, during which the crew for the mission is revealed to the public. This time, one of the three crew members will, for the first time, be an international astronaut. One of two Pakistani astronaut candidates will fly to the Tiangong space station on Shenzhou-24, marking a first both for China's outpost and for Pakistan, which will see one its astronauts reach orbit for the first time. Though public details are sparse, it is thought that the Pakistani astronaut, operating as a payload specialist, will stay aboard Tiangong for around a week, returning home on the departing Shenzhou-23 spacecraft. One of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts — who are approaching the end of their six-month-long mission, having launched on May 24 — will stay aboard Tiangong for another half a year. This will provide the international visitor with a seat home on Shenzhou-23, and allow a Chinese astronaut to make the country's first year-long stay in orbit. This extra-long mission will supply China with data on physiology ahead of crewed lunar flights and other long-duration missions. China approved its human spaceflight program in 1992 and launched its first orbital crewed mission in 2003, with Yang Liwei becoming the first Chinese national in space. The country then completed the three-module Tiangong space station in late 2022 and has kept the orbital outpost constantly crewed ever since, with rotating six-month-long missions with brief handovers between crews. Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed mission and will mark the first time a foreign national is flying on a Shenzhou spacecraft. China is also looking to double the size of Tiangong in the coming years, potentially opening the way to further international missions and space tourist visits.

science.title: Don't miss Saturn shine close to the moon on Nov. 20
science.description: null The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset on Nov. 20, presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby. Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length. Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky. The moon will present a spectacular target through the eyepiece of a 6-inch telescope, as the terminator line separating night from day creeps ever closer to its western edge. It's a great time to explore the 110 km-wide Gassendi Crater on the edge of Mare Humorum as its eastern rim and central peaks throw intense shadows across its interior. Gassendi Crater is a fascinating target for telescope observation during the moon's waxing gibbous phase. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva. Slewing your telescope over to Saturn will reveal details and subtle variations in the cloud surface of the gas giant , along with its iconic ring system, which is gradually becoming more visible following its ring plane crossing in March 2025. science.title: NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars
science.description: 5 min read NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, illustrated here, scans the entire sky every three hours as it orbits Earth. Its publicly available data helps scientists find the rapidly spinning cores of dead stars, known as pulsars. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Chris Smith (USRA/GESTAR) An international team of scientists has developed a method that can find pulsars in publicly available NASA data about a million times faster than before. This opens the door to discovering many more of these rapidly spinning objects. A paper describing the results published Thursday in the Physical Review Letters. Using 15 years of data from NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope and a cryptography-based method developed by study co-authors Dotan Gazith and Barak Zackay from the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel, the team found PSR J1622−7204, an isolated pulsar spinning 261 times per second, using the equivalent of 10 hours of computing time on a standard computer processor. By comparison, the previous best method failed to find the pulsar, despite using enough computing power that a standard processor would take 600 years to perform the calculation. A pulsar is a rapidly spinning neutron star that sweeps beams of radiation toward Earth, much like a lighthouse. Finding pulsars in gamma-ray data is extraordinarily difficult because Fermi detects only a tiny number of photons from a given pulsar, mixed in with background noise from other gamma-ray-emitting sources and the broader universe. To find the signal, researchers must accurately guess several unknowns at once: how fast the star spins, how quickly the spin is slowing down, and precisely where it sits in the sky. Searching every possible combination would require an impossible number of computations. “We don’t see every rotation from the pulsar, and we can’t just count the rotations to work out where the photon came from,” said lead author Daniel Pook-Kolb, a scientist at the Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics (Albert Einstein Institute) in Germany. “We have a four-dimensional grid, and we must search each direction with millions of trials in it. There’s just not enough computing power on Earth to do it.” This artist’s concept shows a pulsar, which emits light in regular pulses as it rotates, like a cosmic lighthouse. Pulsars are dense remnants of exploded stars, and are part of a class of objects called neutron stars. Openly available data from NASA’s Fermi space telescope can help scientists spot pulsars in the gamma-ray spectrum. science.title: Empire State Building glows gold for NASA's Voyager spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 19, 2026
science.description: null The Empire State Building is illuminated in gold to celebrate Voyager 1 hitting one light-day from Earth, seen here on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, from SUMMIT One Vanderbilt in New York City. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display. What is it? Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe. So any signal we send to Voyager 1 or it sends back now takes a full day as the spacecraft continues to explore interstellar space. To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in New York City lit up in gold . This golden glow references the Golden Record onboard both the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft. And the Empire State Building wasn't the only major landmark to celebrate the occasion. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, and both the Willis Tower and the Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois have all been illuminated gold to mark the milestone. Why is it incredible? The Golden Record that these gold glowing buildings are referencing serves as an inanimate ambassador for Earth , carrying information about humanity, our planet, the other species who live here, the languages we speak, the music we listen to and so much more. It even includes instructions for building a record player to play the record. The Voyager mission has, and continues to, make incredible scientific discoveries and observations throughout our solar system and now in interstellar space. But this Golden Record provides an additional aspect to the mission that connects us here on Earth to whatever unknown life may exist out there. If some sort of life forms out in the cosmos were to ever come across Voyager and its Golden Record at any point in the distant future, they might learn a little bit about our small blue dot.

science.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 Makes History Reaching One Light-Day From Earth
science.description: Voyager 1, depicted in this artist’s concept, reached one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, 2026. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, humanity’s farthest-flying spacecraft, has reached one light-day from Earth, after more than 49 years of constant travel. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, equaling about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). The spacecraft achieved the milestone at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST) Nov. 18. Voyager team members at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, managed by Caltech, heard from the probe 24 hours later, the time it took for the spacecraft’s radio signal traveling at the speed of light to reach Earth, early Thursday. “Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. The Voyager mission would be remarkable just for what it contributed to planetary science with the Grand Tour of the outer planets,” said Joe Westlake, director, Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. “But it went on to become central to NASA’s fleet of heliophysics missions offering insights into the star that we all revolve around, the Sun.” Scientists use light to measure the vast distances of space. Light travels at about 186,000 miles (299,000 kilometers) a second in a vacuum. A ray of sunlight passing Earth takes about 1.3 seconds to reach the Moon, about four hours to reach Neptune, and another 20 hours to reach Voyager 1. For comparison, a light-year is 5.88 trillion miles (9.46 trillion kilometers). Even though the team has not received science and engineering data from Voyager 1 since Nov. 14, the spacecraft is sending what is called a carrier signal, which typically conveys that data to Earth. Mission engineers used the carrier signal and trajectory calculations to confirm the light-day milestone. They continue to analyze the issue impacting the science and engineering data. Humanity’s only probes in interstellar space, Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, launched in 1977 to take advantage of a rare planetary alignment. Managed by JPL, they were only the third and fourth spacecraft to visit Jupiter and Saturn, and the first to return high-resolution imagery, transforming our understanding of these worlds and their moons. Voyager 2 went on to study the ethereal ice giants, Neptune and Uranus. Both spacecraft continue to measure changes in the Sun’s magnetic field across vast distances. “Voyager 1 crossing the light-day threshold is yet another historic feat on an extraordinary voyage of discovery,” said Dave Gallagher, JPL director. “Above all, this milestone stands as a testament to the exceptional teams who built, programmed, and fly these spacecraft today, and who have overcome countless challenges to keep them connected to Earth across the vastness of space.
